_link.title: I can describe the three conditions that must be met for a successful collision

toLevel2.stem: What are the three conditions required for a successful collision according to collision theory?
toLevel2.answer: Particles must collide, with sufficient energy, and in the correct orientation
distractors: Particles must be heated, dissolved, and in an open system
Particles must be gases, at high pressure, and at low temperature
Particles must be large, slow-moving, and in a closed system

toLevel2.stem: The first condition of collision theory states that particles must:
distractors: dissolve in a solvent
be in the same phase
have the same mass

toLevel2.stem: The second condition of collision theory states that particles must collide with energy equal to or greater than:
distractors: the enthalpy change
the kinetic energy
the bond energy

toLevel2.stem: The third condition of collision theory states that particles must collide in:
distractors: a closed system
the liquid phase
a straight line

toLevel2.stem: If any one of the three collision theory conditions is not met, the result is:
distractors: a slower reaction occurs
a different product forms
the reaction occurs in reverse

toLevel2.stem: For a reaction to occur, particles must collide with sufficient energy and in the correct orientation.
distractors: False

toLevel2.stem: Reactions occur simply because reactants are present in the same container.
distractors: True

toLevel2.stem: The three conditions for a successful collision are: particles must {{blank:1}}, with sufficient {{blank:2}}, and in the correct orientation.
distractors: dissolve
mass
separate
temperature

toLevel2.stem: Particles must have energy equal to or greater than the {{blank:1}} energy and collide in the correct {{blank:2}}.
distractors: kinetic
direction

temperature

toLevel2.stem: Collision theory explains why reactions do not occur simply because reactants are {{blank:1}} — the quality and {{blank:2}} of collisions matter.
distractors: heated
speed

toLevel3.stem: Why is it not enough for particles to simply collide for a reaction to occur?
toLevel3.answer: They must also have sufficient energy and correct orientation for bonds to break and form
distractors: Collisions always result in reactions regardless of other conditions
Particles never actually collide — reactions happen without contact
Collisions are unnecessary because reactions are driven by temperature alone

toLevel3.stem: What does 'sufficient energy' mean in the context of collision theory?
toLevel3.answer: The combined kinetic energy of the colliding particles meets or exceeds the activation energy
distractors: The particles have any amount of kinetic energy, no matter how small
The total energy of the system is greater than zero at any temperature
The particles are moving at exactly the same speed as each other

toLevel3.stem: Why does correct orientation matter for a reaction to occur?
toLevel3.answer: The reactive parts of the molecules must be aligned for bonds to break and form correctly
distractors: Orientation only matters for solid reactions, not for gases or liquids
Correct orientation reduces the kinetic energy needed for the reaction
Orientation determines the temperature at which the reaction occurs

toLevel3.stem: How do the three conditions of collision theory explain why heating increases reaction rate?
toLevel3.answer: Higher temperature increases kinetic energy, so more collisions exceed Ea, and particles collide more frequently
distractors: Higher temperature improves the orientation of every collision that occurs
Higher temperature eliminates the need for collisions to have sufficient energy
Higher temperature reduces the number of collisions but improves their quality

toLevel3.stem: Which of the three conditions is affected by increasing concentration?
toLevel3.answer: The frequency of collisions (condition 1) — more particles per volume means more collisions
distractors: The energy of collisions (condition 2) — more particles means higher energy per collision
The orientation of collisions (condition 3) — more particles means better alignment
All three conditions are equally affected by increasing concentration

toLevel3.stem: Why do all three conditions need to be met simultaneously for a reaction?
toLevel3.answer: Missing any one condition means the collision cannot overcome the energy barrier or form products
distractors: Only two conditions need to be met — the third is optional
The conditions can be met at different times during the reaction
Meeting one condition very strongly can compensate for missing another

toLevel3.stem: Increasing concentration increases how often particles collide but does not change the energy or orientation of individual collisions.
distractors: False

toLevel3.stem: All three conditions must be met {{blank:1}} — missing any one condition means the collision is {{blank:2}}.
distractors: separately
successful
sequentially
repeated

toLevel3.stem: Heating increases rate by affecting condition {{blank:1}} (more collisions) and condition {{blank:2}} (more particles exceed Ea).
Correct orientation ensures that the {{blank:1}} parts of the molecules are aligned so that {{blank:2}} can break and form.
distractors: outer
atoms
central
electrons

toLevel4.stem: Hydrogen and oxygen gases are mixed at room temperature but do not react. Using collision theory, which condition is most likely not being met?
toLevel4.answer: Condition 2 — most collisions do not have energy equal to or exceeding the high Ea
distractors: Condition 1 — the gas particles are not colliding with each other
Condition 3 — every collision has incorrect orientation at room temperature
All three conditions are being met but the reaction is still not occurring

toLevel4.stem: A spark is needed to ignite a hydrogen-oxygen mixture. Which collision theory condition does the spark address?
toLevel4.answer: It provides the initial energy to overcome the activation energy barrier
distractors: It aligns the particles in the correct orientation for reaction
It creates new hydrogen and oxygen particles for the reaction
It removes the need for particles to collide with each other

toLevel4.stem: A student increases the temperature of a reaction. Which of the three conditions are improved?
toLevel4.answer: Conditions 1 and 2 — collisions are more frequent and more energetic
distractors: Only condition 3 — orientation improves at higher temperature
All three conditions — temperature improves every aspect equally
Only condition 1 — temperature only increases collision frequency

toLevel4.stem: A catalyst is added to a reaction. Which of the three conditions is affected?
toLevel4.answer: Condition 2 — the activation energy threshold is lowered so more collisions have sufficient energy
distractors: Condition 1 — the catalyst increases the frequency of collisions
Condition 3 — the catalyst improves the orientation of all collisions
All three conditions are equally improved by the catalyst

toLevel4.stem: A student grinds a solid reactant into powder. Which of the three conditions is improved?
toLevel4.answer: Condition 1 — more surface particles are available for collisions
distractors: Condition 2 — each particle gains more kinetic energy
Condition 3 — grinding improves the orientation of every collision
Conditions 2 and 3 — grinding affects energy and orientation

toLevel4.stem: A scientist observes that two reactants collide frequently and with high energy, but the reaction rate is still very low. Which condition most likely limits the rate?
toLevel4.answer: Condition 3 — the orientation requirement may be very strict
distractors: Condition 1 — the particles are not colliding often enough
Condition 2 — the particles do not have enough energy
All three conditions are being met so the rate should be high

toLevel4.stem: A student increases the concentration of a reactant. Which condition of collision theory is directly improved?
toLevel4.answer: Condition 1 — more particles per volume leads to more frequent collisions
distractors: Condition 2 — each particle has more kinetic energy at higher concentration
Condition 3 — particles orient more correctly at higher concentration
All three conditions improve equally with increased concentration

toLevel4.stem: A spark ignites a H₂/O₂ mixture by providing the initial {{blank:1}} to overcome the {{blank:2}} energy barrier.
distractors: heat
kinetic
force
potential

toLevel4.stem: Grinding a solid improves condition {{blank:1}} (collision frequency) by exposing more {{blank:2}} particles.
distractors: internal
dissolved

toLevel4.stem: A catalyst improves condition {{blank:1}} by lowering the activation energy, while temperature improves conditions {{blank:2}} and 2.

toLevel5.stem: A student analyzes why different rate-affecting factors target different collision theory conditions. Temperature affects conditions 1 and 2; concentration affects condition 1; catalysts affect condition 2. What does this analysis reveal?
toLevel5.answer: Each factor has a specific mechanism that targets particular aspects of collision theory
distractors: All factors affect all three conditions equally but through different mechanisms
Only temperature affects collision theory conditions; other factors are irrelevant
The conditions of collision theory are independent and cannot be analysed separately

toLevel5.stem: A student claims: 'If we could guarantee correct orientation for every collision, all we would need is sufficient energy for 100% reaction rate.' Evaluate this claim.
toLevel5.answer: Mostly correct — with perfect orientation, the rate would depend entirely on what fraction of collisions exceed Ea
distractors: Incorrect — orientation has no effect on reaction rate at all
Incorrect — perfect orientation would prevent any reactions from occurring
Correct — but perfect orientation can be achieved by increasing temperature

toLevel5.stem: Compare how a catalyst and a temperature increase each address the three conditions differently. Which analysis is correct?
toLevel5.answer: A catalyst lowers the Ea threshold (condition 2); temperature increases particle energy (condition 2) and collision frequency (condition 1)
distractors: Both affect condition 3 (orientation) through different mechanisms
A catalyst affects condition 1; temperature affects condition 3
Both affect all three conditions equally but to different degrees

toLevel5.stem: A peer argues: 'Condition 1 (particles must collide) is trivial and not worth mentioning — of course particles collide.' Why is this condition still important?
toLevel5.answer: It underpins the role of concentration, surface area, and pressure — all of which increase collision frequency
distractors: The peer is correct — condition 1 is unnecessary and should be removed
Condition 1 is only important for reactions in a vacuum where collisions do not occur
Condition 1 only matters for solid-state reactions and is irrelevant for gases

toLevel5.stem: No factor commonly studied at VCE level directly improves condition 3 (orientation). What does this tell us about orientation?
toLevel5.answer: Orientation is an inherent property of each collision that cannot be externally controlled by typical rate factors
distractors: Orientation is not a real condition and should be removed from collision theory
Temperature directly controls orientation but this is not taught at VCE level
Catalysts directly control orientation by rotating molecules into the correct position

toLevel5.stem: A student creates a table mapping each rate factor to the collision theory conditions it affects. This table shows that temperature is unique. Why?
toLevel5.answer: Temperature is the only common factor that affects two conditions simultaneously (frequency and energy)
distractors: Temperature is the only factor that does not affect any collision theory condition
Temperature affects all three conditions while other factors affect only one
Temperature and concentration both affect two conditions, so neither is unique

toLevel5.stem: In designing an industrial process, a chemist wants to maximise the rate. Using the three conditions, what combination of strategies would be most effective?
toLevel5.answer: Increase concentration (condition 1), use a catalyst (condition 2), and increase temperature moderately (conditions 1 and 2)
distractors: Only increase temperature because it is the only factor that affects rate
Only add a catalyst because it affects all three conditions simultaneously
Only increase concentration because collision frequency is the most important factor

toLevel5.stem: A student asks: 'Is there a fourth condition of collision theory?' Based on VCE chemistry, what is the best response?
toLevel5.answer: No — the three conditions (collision, sufficient energy, correct orientation) are comprehensive for VCE level
distractors: Yes — the fourth condition is that the system must be closed
Yes — the fourth condition is that a catalyst must be present
Yes — the fourth condition is that the reaction must be exothermic

distractors: one
two

toLevel5.stem: Condition 1 underpins the role of {{blank:1}}, surface area, and pressure, while condition 2 underpins the role of temperature and {{blank:2}}.
